key_insight: Realistic Lindbladian noise makes Pauli-fidelity asymmetries between a Pauli operator and its gate-conjugate highly constrained, so the gauge can be fixed using the noise type rather than its unknown strength.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical route to cleaner quantum calibration and error mitigation by separating SPAM from gate noise more reliably in hardware characterization workflows.
method: Use Lindbladian perturbation theory to analyze symmetry breaking in Pauli fidelities for Clifford gates.
Derive first-order selection rules showing coherent errors preserve symmetry while only certain off-diagonal dissipative errors can break it.
Exploit approximate symmetry constraints to fix gauge and identify SPAM errors from the error class alone.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports both numerical validation and experimental confirmation on IBM Kingston across a broad set of gates including ZZπ/2, CZ, CNOT, iSWAP, and SWAP.
watch_item: The symmetry-based gauge fixing is approximate and depends on the assumed noise model, so mismatched error-class assumptions could bias characterization.
paper_title: Symmetries of Pauli Noise from Lindbladian Dynamics
